Second review: 892444f9cd35 / 14a9173d4ca7 / 10ae44308fa3

Judgements (independent of reputation and classifier scores)

892444f9cd352edffa2c80eb3e8b9af15440d9b9820dae67bdbf094c5a2d7aa8
Blihan Windows HTTP task loader, recovered PE image: MALICIOUS.
Entry 401000 reads its own image, prepares a Windows-directory microsofthelp.exe
copy, calls the Run-key writer at 401a70, and launches that path via 401e00.
The Run-key function opens HKCU's CurrentVersion\\Run and conditionally writes
the executable path. The loader checks a mutex and installation marker.
401270 repeatedly retrieves response records, checks length and magic 0x1e240
at +0x40, and decodes the record body with an inline 64-byte XOR key (401490).
4014d0 walks typed records at +0x48. Polling-thread code beginning at 401930
passes the URL from a type-0x200 record to 401610. That path retrieves bytes,
generates an eight-letter .exe path, checks MZ, writes and closes the response,
and calls the executable-path launch helper. Another task path opens hidden IE
visits, waits and terminates the child; adapter bytes supply a MAC query field.
401510 stages/loads HidePlugin.dll and resolves/calls WindowsHookExON; that
export name does not establish keylogging or cross-process injection.
The paired mutex/registry and protocol evidence supports Blihan attribution.
The HTTP task dispatcher, executable delivery, and unsolicited install/autorun
behavior tip the decision. This is not an ordinary installer or HTTP client.

This supplied image already contains readable code under MPRESS section labels.
Those labels do not establish an active packed payload. Import recovery is
broken: indirect-call slots retain unbound RVAs, and no DLL imports are recovered.
The configuration offset in the self-file header is zero. No working C2 endpoint
or successful execution is established. These limitations affect operational
success, not the purpose of the recovered malicious implementation. No native
code was run. All 55 original reported findings and both hostile findings remain.

14a9173d4ca74002727c3382e92865332de4a01967816eecbb62796840ad134d
Solana-account rendezvous and native COFF module loader: MALICIOUS.
resolve_stage_server POSTs getAccountInfo JSON, selects its data value, Base64
decodes it, applies a repeating five-byte XOR, and returns the resulting host.
main formats that host into an HTTPS URL, obtains object bytes, and passes the
same bytes to execute_coff_module. That routine checks AMD64 COFF fields, copies
sections into RWX memory, applies relocations, resolves an entry symbol, and
calls it. This is an opaque blockchain-selected executable stage, with no
verification or user-selected module interface. The covert rendezvous feeding
unrestricted native execution tips the decision over a normal COFF utility.

The account is a placeholder, six helpers have declarations only, and mapping
bounds/null checks are incomplete. This is illustrative/incomplete attack
source, not a demonstrated working implant. A disclosed training or authorized
red-team purpose could affect deployment interpretation; none is supplied.
These facts do not turn the explicit loading workflow into ordinary wallet use.
The verdict does not depend on reaching the final payload or compiling this file.

10ae44308fa3ccbf56375ceb57d948b5679af63e995b44e1dfc877ee71c18d40
NDSJ/NDSW-style (Parrot-TDS-associated) browser-loader fragment: MALICIOUS.
Independent decoding reproduces custom Base64-alphabet decoding, RC4 KSA/PRGA,
and 18 string-table rotations. The resolved logic normalizes a www. prefix and
requires a nonempty external referrer and an empty document.cookie. It issues
an asynchronous GET to storage.webfiledata.com/ui_static.js?ver=<random token>.
Only a completed status-200 response containing the ndsx marker is passed to
window.eval. There is no cookie theft: cookies gate activation, not transmission.
No second-stage content was retrieved and no assertion about that stage is made.
Concealed remote evaluation and visitor cloaking, unrelated to the visible React
render tail, establish an injected loader component rather than a React utility.
The decision is based on recovered logic; guard names and reputation alone are
not the basis for it. Exact family attribution beyond this loader lineage is
not established.

The supplied file begins mid-bundle and fails standalone JavaScript parsing.
The entire implant follows //# sourceMappingURL on the same physical line and
is comment content. No Unicode line terminator or other comment escape activates
it. Thus the exact supplied fragment cannot execute this loader as JavaScript.
This is a malicious implant fragment, not evidence of a working infected release.
A QuickJS check compiled the original without invoking it (SyntaxError); a
separately extracted payload was exercised only against in-memory mocks.
The mocks recorded GET/eval for an external referrer and no cookies; same-host
referrers, any cookie, empty referrers and unmarked responses suppressed their
respective stages. window.eval was a recorder and XMLHttpRequest never used a
network. A research-fixture origin is possible but no such provenance accompanies
these bytes. The content would still warrant incident investigation on a host.

Rule corrections and preservation

The old source-map/encrypted-payload rule proved only an RC4 obfuscator and
appended source-map text. It did not establish execution or a compromised trusted
release. Its exact matcher, scopes, confidence, and exclusions are preserved as
suspicious anti-static/obfuscator evidence under source-map-comment-with-rc4-
obfuscator. Its old hostile supply-chain claim is removed. An ordinary commented
RC4 example reproduces the overclaim, but that synthetic control is not the sole
basis: the actual original is fully commented and syntactically truncated.
Every original suspicious observation remains, and the source-map observation
remains suspicious as well. The active extracted payload retains obfuscation
findings without needing a source-map concatenation. Missing fully decoded
fetch/eval and referrer findings are a string-table recovery limitation, not
justification for ciphertext-specific duplicate signatures.

The old hostile COFF composite checked parsing, RWX allocation, memcpy, and an
arbitrary module_init label. It did not require calling the entry or receiving a
payload. A caller-selected local COFF utility and a parser-only variant therefore
matched an unsupported execution/hostility claim. The revised neutral loader
query binds the downloaded buffer to a local loader parameter, copies from that
parameter into the same RWX allocation supplied to symbol resolution, and binds
the resolved entry to its guarded invocation. The native endpoint query binds
HTTP response -> account data -> Base64 output -> XOR destination -> returned
host -> snprintf authority -> GET URL across resolver/main definitions.
Solana C2 now requires that linkage plus executable-loader admission. The
separate module-execution objective moves to execution/payload/module-load.
Neither rule gates on a URL path, account spelling or entry-symbol label.
The renamed fixture changes all three plus local function/variable names and
retains both hostile results. A no-entry-call and an unrelated-authority control
lose unsupported convictions while retaining their true neutral operations.
COFF is loaded through a custom object-module runtime, not injected into another
process; no process-injection or privilege-escalation claim is added.

The C XOR-assignment matcher is unchanged and remains notable, but moves from
encode/xor to encoding/xor: it establishes a modulo-indexed XOR operand, not a
loop, key, or encoding direction. The broad XOR transform group, exact staging
consumer, and broad paste-site consumer retain its alternative. The other broad
encode consumer is PHP-only and has no overlap. The native XOR/modulo metric
moves from crypto to arithmetic without changing scopes, confidence, exclusions
or matcher. It cannot prove a key or cipher. Exact consumers, including Go
string-recovery and existing WebSocket-unmask fixture expectations, are updated.
Root crypto consumers are PowerShell-only or PE-only and cannot have matched
this source-only fact; no cipher evidence is removed from them.

Three PE section-type/field observations move from filesystem section handling
to PE parser/executable-header homes with their exact matchers, scopes and
criticalities retained. All explicit consumers and same-leaf references are
updated. No ancestor fs/file/section selector selects these atoms. A broader fs
selector cannot legitimately infer file I/O from a PE field reference. The
VirtualAlloc description now says API reference because source projections also
match ordinary API calls, not only imports. Network, decoding, RWX and native
execution findings remain notable or higher. The engine emits the WinHTTP header
import at baseline; this import fact is not a call and is not shadowed by YAML.

Consumer search included each moved ID and every ancestor; the saved initial
consumer record is in scratch/consumers.json. Source-map and COFF rules had no
explicit or ancestor consumers. Other exact consumers are visible in the diff.
The source-map and COFF technique observations remain; no technique is deleted
based solely on a synthetic near miss. Existing attack fixtures outside the
batch (RC4 gate loader, Ethereum dead-drop socket stage, compressed-source
evaluation) retain every hostile/suspicious result. The compact RPC client stays
free of hostile/suspicious results; WebSocket unmasking keeps its neutral XOR
observation. check.py checks positive/negative bindings and scan comparisons.

Scans, classifier disagreements, and coverage limits

atomscan and cleave facts were run on every original; all facts report no archive
members and final scans contain one analysis unit each. Re-scans use the full
local trait tree, without dependency following, remote uploads or rule refresh.
Initial scans hit the installed validator's stale naming-directory budget. For
analysis only CLEAVE_VALIDATE=0 bypasses that old lint gate; the final validation
uses the newer local release binary, whose source contains the reviewed budget.
No rule was changed to accommodate that tool mismatch. The final make validate
result is recorded in the task output. No inline YARA rules were edited.

comparison.json records exact before/after results and probabilities:
- PE: 0.999440 -> 0.999440, level 15000 unchanged; all native model cls fields
  are 0. Two hostile rules are intact. Default calibrated native classification
  disagrees with the malicious judgement; only a loose level flags it.
- C: 0.998858 -> 0.995969, level 1 unchanged, source model cls=2. Two hostile
  results remain, with corrected linkage/placement and additional neutral facts.
- JS: 0.998330, level 1 -> 0.996623, level -1, all final model cls fields 0.
  Removing the unsupported hostile supply-chain inference exposes a classifier
  miss despite four suspicious findings and the recovered implant logic.
The model bundle is v18.18 and warns that its v18 feature specification treats
newer v19 features as zero. No inaccurate rule or duplicate was restored to
influence those probabilities.

Remaining context limits: no registry identity/version or deployment authority
was supplied; the per-hash registry map has no entries for these three hashes.
There is no assertion of external feed/advisory corroboration. C and JS facts
also explicitly report limited/incomplete flow graphs. Native import repair,
full RC4-table recovery, model retraining and final-stage identification are
engine/research gaps rather than fabricated YAML behavior.

Validation follow-up: the arithmetic leaf reached 101 rules. The full effective
rule inventory was audited (arithmetic-leaf-audit.json); there were no exact
duplicates to erase. One existing atom matched x86 byte-memory comparison text,
not scalar arithmetic or code-integrity verification. Its exact matcher, scope,
confidence and notable severity move to mem/compare as assembly-byte-memory-
immediate-compare. It has no exact or ancestor arithmetic consumers. Positive
byte-memory and negative register-only controls verify that distinction. All
100 other arithmetic observations remain, with no new partition or budget
exception. Description lengths and a redundant scope declaration were also fixed.
